title: What Is System Design?
sources: TechCrunch, 'WhatsApp is now delivering roughly 100 billion messages a day' (2020-10-29): Mark Zuckerberg said WhatsApp now delivers about 100 billion messages a day

Design Gurus, 'What is called system design?' / Educative, 'I'm new to System Design, where do I start?': system design = defining the architecture, components, data and how they interact so a system meets its requirements, incl. scalability (many servers, load balancers, caches)

lines.text: How does one app serve millions of people at the same time?
lines.caps: HOW DOES *ONE APP | SERVE *MILLIONS | AT THE *SAME | *TIME?

lines.text: Your phone talks to a computer called a server,
and one server is like one cook in a tiny kitchen.
lines.caps: AND ONE *SERVER | IS *LIKE | ONE *COOK | IN A *TINY | *KITCHEN

lines.text: But WhatsApp delivers around a hundred billion messages a day,
and one cook would totally melt.
So you plan it like a restaurant chain:
a host who sends each guest to a free table,
and popular dishes kept ready to grab.
picking the pieces and how they fit together,
so the app stays fast when the whole world shows up.
lines.caps: SO THE *APP | STAYS *FAST | WHEN THE *WHOLE | *WORLD | *SHOWS UP

lines.text: That's day one. Tomorrow: client versus server.
